analysis.title: Tech earnings face the returns test (UBS House View - Daily Asia)
key_insights: Tech stocks traded choppy on Tuesday ahead of mega-cap earnings. Meta reports Wednesday and starts the US mega-cap tech reporting season.
Rising interest rates and higher financing costs mean investors want evidence that AI can drive meaningful monetization and returns that justify elevated capex and pressure on free cash flow.
Three areas to watch: health of core businesses (advertising, software, devices, digital commerce), AI monetization beyond adoption, and tangible returns on the spending cycle.
Core business strength funds AI investment and cushions earnings while AI revenue develops. The question is whether recent growth rates hold against tougher comparisons and macro risks.
Potential AI monetization models include subscriptions, consumption-based pricing, advertising, transactions and higher cloud utilization. Clarity on pricing and willingness to pay is needed.
Investors will focus on capacity utilization, pricing power, capital requirements and returns on AI investment. Management commentary on the future pace of capex will shape 2027 expectations.
UBS expects a strong Q3 tech earnings season fundamentally, but elevated expectations may cause company-specific volatility.

UBS stays constructive on the structural AI opportunity and sees opportunities in hyperscalers and high-quality semiconductor and hardware beneficiaries. It also suggests defensive tech exposure and rebalancing of concentrated tech positions across sectors and regions.
UBS suggests structured strategies for tech: capital preservation structures, or yield-generating structures that sell volatility and offer a chance to buy favored tech names at lower prices.

France unrest adds to sovereign pressure. Localized curfews followed a weekend of riots with around 2,400 arrests and nearly 1,000 police officers injured. Macron rejected Interior Minister Nuñez's offer to resign.
France's 10-year yield rose to 4.9260% on Tuesday. The French-German 10-year spread is near 150 basis points, a level associated with the Eurozone debt crisis, and EURUSD trades at 1.12.

UBS expects global bond yields to move lower over coming months, but French fiscal and political challenges could keep European sovereign markets volatile. The deficit is well above the level needed to stabilize debt, and a parliament without a majority makes consolidation harder.
Mitigants against broader stress: well-capitalized French banks, limited domestic sovereign holdings, and Europe's institutional safeguards.

UBS keeps a positive view on global bonds, favoring short- to intermediate-term maturities and high quality investment grade, and is cautious on the longest maturities. It expects EURUSD to recover toward 1.16 by year-end and sees selective opportunities to sell euro downside risk for yield against the US dollar and Swiss franc.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong core businesses in advertising, software, devices and digital commerce fund AI investment, and UBS expects a strong fundamental Q3 tech season with structural AI demand intact.
tension_points.bear_case: Rising rates and higher financing costs raise the bar for AI returns, while elevated capex pressures free cash flow and elevated expectations may cause company-specific volatility.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Management commentary showing weak AI monetization or capex pace rising without clear returns, and core-business growth failing to hold against tougher comparisons.

tension_points.bull_case: Well-capitalized French banks, limited domestic sovereign holdings and Europe's institutional safeguards reduce the risk of a broader financial crisis. Market pressure could push parties toward a fiscal agreement.
tension_points.bear_case: The deficit is well above the debt-stabilizing level and a parliament without a majority makes credible consolidation hard, keeping European sovereign markets volatile.
